title: Factcheck: 18 misleading myths about heat pumps
summary: Carbon Brief fact-check rebutting UK myths on heat pumps: cold weather, insulation, running costs, lifespan, emissions and upfront cost.

assertions.quote: Heat pumps can work in any building if sized, designed and installed correctly.
These three countries have the highest heat pump sales per 1,000 households on the continent.
In all three countries, there are now more than 40 heat pumps per 100 households, more than in any other country in the world.
when temperatures drop to as low as -20C, a standard air-source heat pump can still operate with a COP of around 2.
heat pumps use electricity to gather extra heat from the outside air or ground, meaning they typically generate at least 2 units of heat
a heat pump would cut CO2 emissions by 77-86% over 15 years compared with a gas boiler
heat pumps can last a couple decades or even longer.
well-designed systems can save UK households hundreds of pounds a year, even though electricity is more expensive than gas.
The running costs of heat pumps relative to gas boilers depend on energy prices and the efficiency of the heat pump installation.
heat pump users can lower their operating costs through using dedicated tariffs.
households can save £110 per year by disconnecting from the gas grid and no longer paying the gas “standing charge”.
It is true that heat pumps are more expensive to buy than gas boilers.
The evidence suggests the opposite: heat pumps increase the value of properties.

verdicts.note: Edwards notes in passing, citing other work, that homes with heat pumps may sell at a price premium.
